findings.message: AC-1 says one rule decides "has no owner", but the screens still use their own rule: `ownerName` is missing. `ProposalPage.tsx:31` (the warn chip), `ProposalsPage.tsx:145`, `ProjectPage.tsx:55-57` and the update card's From line (`proposal-card.ts:90,96`) each show "Unassigned" when `owner_name` is null. `hasNoOwner` treats a row with only a user as owned. So the page contradicts the Unassigned chip, the pin and the agent on that row, which is one of AC-1's own four test cases. Fix: show the chip and the label through `hasNoOwner(p)`, and when the row has a user but no name, show the user's name instead of "Unassigned". Add the screens to the AC-1 table test.
findings.scenario: A proposal with owner_user_id = Maya and owner_name = null → the proposal page shows the warn chip "Unassigned". needsOf gives no "unassigned", the pin offers no "Make me the owner", and the agent suggests no owner.

findings.message: The fix adds another inline copy of "is withdrawn" (`p.withdrawn_at || meta?.withdrawn`, which tests meta for truthiness) beside the existing helper `withdrawn()` in `lifecycle.ts:26` (`meta.withdrawn === true`), `services.ts:43`, `agent.ts:25` and the SQL `ACTIVE`/contract rule (`meta->>'withdrawn' = 'true'`). These copies already read different meta values differently. Fix: export one predicate (beside `hasNoOwner` in readiness.ts, or the lifecycle helper) and call it here and in `services.ts:43`.
findings.scenario: meta = {"withdrawn": "false"} (a string) → mark_task_done refuses "was withdrawn", while update_proposal and withdraw_proposal (lifecycle `=== true`) treat the same proposal as open. meta = {"withdrawn": 1} → tasks.ts refuses, lifecycle allows, and the contract SQL says it isn't withdrawn.

findings.message: AC-7 adds the `unavailable` code to `userFacing` in `@amax/mcp/registry.ts`, but the REST error mapper doesn't know it. It falls through to `409 refused`, so a temporary "module switched off, retry later" reads as a permanent conflict and loses its code. Fix: map `code === "unavailable"` to 503 with `error: "unavailable"` (and a Retry-After if wanted), and add a REST test for it next to the not_found and invalid_input cases.
findings.scenario: With Time switched off, a REST call that resolves a proposal time-line pin (get_proposal_event with line time:1) → HTTP 409 {error:"refused"} instead of 503 {error:"unavailable"}. A client that retries 5xx and drops 409 never retries.

findings.message: AC-10 promises that Time's migrations run with Delivery off. Dropping the FK in a later migration doesn't deliver that: `0009_entry_proposal.sql:3` still runs `references delivery.proposal(id)` on every fresh install, so the migration fails before 0010 can drop the key. 0009 hasn't merged yet (it's in PR #113, which 087 builds on), so remove the `references` clause from 0009 itself and keep 0010 as an `if exists` drop for databases that already ran it. `0001_time.sql:31` also references `delivery.project(id)`, which is the same cross-schema tie and was already there before this diff.
findings.scenario: A fresh database with AMAX_MODULES_DISABLED=delivery, or Time's migrations running before Delivery's → 0009 fails with 'relation "delivery.proposal" does not exist', and Time never installs.

findings.message: The "withdrawn by the repo" case writes `meta = '{"withdrawn": true}'` straight into the table instead of driving the sync import (`sync/import.ts:82`), which is the real path that withdraws a spec proposal. It also replaces the whole meta, so `source` and the other meta stay as a hand-made row has them. Drive it through the import of a spec proposal whose folder is gone.

Partial is reported whenever the loop reaches its tenth batch with a full previous page, even when that page was the last row. It also tells a viewer who may see none of the lines that there are more than 2,000 hidden rows ("Only the newest time lines are shown" over an empty list). Fix: fetch BATCH+1 rows, or probe for one more row, before saying partial. Word the note for the case where nothing is visible.
findings.scenario: Exactly 2,000 time audit rows on a proposal → every viewer sees "older ones weren't read" although all of them were read.

findings.message: The AC-6 test's `finally` resets the installed list to ["delivery","time"] instead of the value it had before. If the suite started unset (null, where the table check decides), every later test in the file now runs with an explicit list. Save the prior list and restore it, or reset it in afterEach.
